question: Which of the following antitussive can lead to hallucinations
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Dextromethorphan" -> "NMDA receptor antagonist" -> "increased risk of dissociative effects" -> "possible hallucinations" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Diphenhydramine" -> "anticholinergic properties" -> "CNS effects including confusion" -> "possible hallucinations" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Morphine" -> "opioid receptor agonist" -> "CNS depression" -> "possible altered mental status" -> "possible hallucinations" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Aprepitant" -> "substance P/neurokinin 1 receptor antagonist" -> "not commonly associated with hallucinations" -> "unlikely to cause hallucinations" -> 20%
analysis: Dextromethorphan is known to act as an NMDA receptor antagonist, which can lead to dissociative effects and hallucinations, especially at higher doses. This is well-documented in the literature. Diphenhydramine, while primarily an antihistamine, has anticholinergic properties that can also lead to CNS effects, including confusion and hallucinations, particularly in sensitive populations or at high doses. Morphine can cause altered mental status and hallucinations, but this is less common compared to the other two. Aprepitant is not associated with hallucinations. Given the evidence, Dextromethorphan is the most recognized antitussive linked to hallucinations, with Diphenhydramine also being a potential but less common cause. Therefore, the best-supported option is Dextromethorphan.
